children: supernatural horror thriller “Other Mommy” scared up an estimated $27.5 million in domestic ticket sales over the weekend, leading the North American box office as moviegoing revenue for 2026 surpassed $8 billion.

The film, starring Jessica Chastain and directed by Rob Savage, opened in 3,365 theaters for an average of $8,172 per location, according to estimates released Sunday by Paul Dergarabedian, head of marketplace trends at Rentrak. International audiences contributed another $17.69 million across 50 territories, bringing the movie’s worldwide opening to $45.19 million.

“Other Mommy,” which follows an eight-year-old girl who develops a relationship with a sinister entity resembling her mother, led a weekend that generated an estimated $85.16 million in domestic ticket sales. That represented a 15.6% decline from the previous weekend but an 18.5% increase from the comparable period last year.

“Verity,” starring Dakota Johnson and Anne Hathaway, finished second with $11.48 million in its second weekend, a 64% decline. The psychological thriller has earned $53.86 million domestically and $113.8 million worldwide. The studio said Hurricane Isaias appeared to affect Saturday attendance in the South and South Central regions, where the film has attracted a significant share of its predominantly female audience.

“Resident Evil” placed third with $8.35 million domestically, bringing its four-week North American total to $138.53 million. The horror franchise also reached a worldwide milestone, generating $320.2 million in cumulative ticket sales, a series record. A $40.6 million opening in China helped drive international weekend revenue of $54.3 million.
“Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt, followed in fourth place with $7.1 million, bringing its domestic total to $49.66 million and worldwide earnings to $131.36 million.

“The Social Reckoning,” written and directed by Aaron Sorkin, debuted in fifth place with $5.5 million from 2,606 theaters. The drama about Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen and journalist Jeff Horwitz also earned $3.5 million internationally across 29 markets, giving it a worldwide opening of $9 million.
The domestic box office crossed the $8 billion threshold on Friday, October 9, reaching $8.073 billion through Sunday, according to Dergarabedian.

That compares with $6.751 billion during the corresponding period in 2025, representing a 19.6% year-over-year increase. The milestone underscores the theatrical industry's recovery in 2026, with domestic ticket sales running more than $1.32 billion ahead of last year's pace.
“Digger,” starring Tom Cruise, fell 60% in its second weekend to $3.2 million. The film, directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu, has earned $14.43 million domestically and $35.3 million worldwide.
“The Odyssey,” directed by Christopher Nolan, remained in the top 10 in its 13th weekend, earning another $2 million domestically. Its North American cumulative total reached $622.97 million.
theaters generated an estimated $16.5 million worldwide over the weekend, an increase of 64% from the comparable period last year.
“Resident Evil” led the premium-format network with $8.8 million, including $7.7 million from China. Its worldwide IMAX total has reached $32.8 million.
“The Odyssey” added another $4.3 million in global IMAX ticket sales following an expansion of its premium-screen footprint, bringing its cumulative IMAX revenue to $546.2 million.

Special-event programming also contributed to the weekend's results. The restored concert film “Queen Budapest,” featuring the band's 1986 performance in Hungary, generated $1.4 million in worldwide IMAX revenue during a limited two-day engagement.

The next major IMAX release is “Street Fighter,” which begins special fan screenings Thursday ahead of its opening weekend. The network also plans to show the concert film “Always Lalisa,” featuring BLACKPINK member LISA, along with additional international releases.

The weekend's results suggest that horror films, established franchises and premium-format screenings continue to attract theatrical audiences as the industry heads into the final quarter of the year.

title: ‘Other Mommy’ tops weekend box office with $27M, domestic ticket sales cross $8B
